CHAPTER 3

Writing Code
编写代码

Any fool can write code that a computer can understand. Good programmers write code that humans can understand.
——Martin Fowler, British software developer, author, and international public speaker on software development

任何傻瓜都能写出计算机能懂的代码。优秀的程序员写出的是人类能读懂的代码。
——Martin Fowler，英国软件开发者、作家、软件开发国际演讲人

Writing code is, without a doubt, a very important part of software engineering. And while the act of coding is widely taught, the nuances of writing good code aren’t as evenly distributed. Just because you can write code to solve a problem doesn’t mean you should write code to solve a problem!1 With the advent of artificial intelligence and agentic coding tools, the job of a software engineer is evolving to one with less hands-on development work and more bug fixing, correcting, and reviewing code generated by an eager AI tool. However, to be good at reviewing code, you must be good at writing code. It may seem counterintuitive, but writing good, clean code is an invaluable skill in the world of AI.

毫无疑问，写代码是软件工程中非常重要的一环。尽管写代码这个动作被广泛教授，但“怎样写好代码”的细微差别却没有被均匀地传授。你能写出解决某个问题的代码，并不意味着你就该写代码去解决那个问题！1随着人工智能和智能体编码工具的出现，软件工程师的工作正在演变：亲手写的代码少了，修 bug、纠正和评审那个跃跃欲试的 AI 工具生成的代码多了。然而，要擅长评审代码，你必须先擅长写代码。这看似反直觉，但在 AI 时代，写出干净优雅的代码是一项无比宝贵的技能。

1 AI doesn’t currently, and likely never will, distinguish between whether it can write code to solve a problem and whether it should.
AI 目前（而且很可能永远）不会区分“它能不能写代码解决一个问题”和“它该不该写代码解决那个问题”。

For better or worse, developers often have strong opinions on what constitutes good code or bad code, but metrics and tooling can give you insights and guidance. Tests are some of the best documentation money can buy. Code reviews, done well, can ensure that your team doesn’t rely on error-prone forms or overly clever code. Ultimately, code should be written to be read by humans.

不管好坏，开发者对什么是好代码、什么是坏代码往往有强烈主张，但指标和工具能给你洞见和指引。测试是金钱能买到的最好的文档之一。做得好的代码评审，能确保你的团队不依赖易错的写法或过于聪明的代码。归根结底，代码是写给人读的。

Despite how it is often taught, programming is first and foremost a communication activity—and not just between the coder and the compiler. Don’t forget, the computer understands any code (at least if it’s syntactically correct), but that doesn’t mean a human will follow what you’re trying to accomplish. The best software engineers focus on writing code that can be understood by the humans reading it. This means that your code needs to be concise and well-organized. The code should clearly communicate its intent so a human can figure out what the code is supposed to do. If it’s easy to read, it’ll be easy to maintain, which is crucial for the long-term success of a software project.

尽管编程常被那样教，但它首先是一种沟通活动——而且不只是编码者与编译器之间的沟通。别忘了，计算机能理解任何代码（至少在语法正确时），但这并不意味着人能跟上你想做的事。最优秀的软件工程师专注于写出读代码的人能理解的代码。这意味着你的代码需要简洁、组织良好。代码应当清晰地传达意图，让人能看出它本该做什么。代码易读，就易维护，而这对一个软件项目的长期成功至关重要。

The first thing you learn when you set out down the path of software development is how to code. Probably with “Hello World!” What is not always taught, whether in an undergrad course, boot camp, or self-led tutorial, is what makes code good, how to write good code, and when to write code to solve a problem. This chapter aims to fill that gap.

踏上软件开发之路时，你学的第一件事是怎么写代码。大概就是从“Hello World！”开始。而无论是本科课程、训练营还是自学教程，并不总会教你：什么造就好代码、怎样写好代码、以及什么时候才该写代码去解决问题。本章旨在填补这个空白。

Don’t Reinvent the Wheel

Before you start pounding out line after line of (undoubtedly excellent) code, take some time to see if the problem at hand has already been solved. Developers often write too much code, solving problems that others have already worked out. Before cranking out some fresh code, look around. Is there a library you could leverage? That isn’t a license to add things ad hoc; don’t forget to analyze those libraries’ dependencies. Be sure to follow your organization’s policies and procedures surrounding third-party libraries.

在你开始一行行敲出（无疑很出色的）代码之前，先花点时间看看手头这个问题是不是已经被解决过了。开发者常常写太多代码，去解决别人早已解决的问题。在产出新代码之前，先四下看看：有没有可以借力的库？但这并不是让你随便加依赖；别忘了分析那些库的依赖。务必遵守公司关于第三方库的政策和流程。

Double-check your primary programming language. Is there a language feature you could use? Languages evolve (see “The Capitalization Assignment” on page 6); five minutes of searching could save you hours of effort. What about your application frameworks? If you think there should be a better way, there just might be. Ask yourself, are you the first person in the universe who has ever written code like this? Odds are you are not (see “Embrace the Lazy Programmer Ethos” on page 5).

再想想你的主力编程语言。有没有可以用上的语言特性？语言在演进（见第 6 页“大小写转换任务”）；搜 5 分钟可能省你几小时。那你的应用框架呢？如果你觉得“应该有更好的办法”，那多半真有。问问自己：我是全宇宙第一个写这种代码的人吗？多半不是（见第 5 页“拥抱懒程序员信条”）。

Before you invest time in writing a new piece of code, it can help to ask yourself a series of questions. Christopher M. Judd teaches the following decision tree in his boot camps (modify for your language and frameworks):

在投入时间写新代码之前，问自己一连串问题会有帮助。Christopher M. Judd 在他的训练营里教下面这棵决策树（请按你的语言和框架调整）：

  • Is this being done anywhere in the current codebase?当前代码库里有没有人已经在做这件事？
  • Does the JDK already do it?JDK 已经能做吗？
  • Are there any Spring Framework or Spring Boot projects that solve this problem?有没有 Spring Framework 或 Spring Boot 的项目已经解决了这个问题？
  • Does a solution exist in Google Guava?Google Guava 里有现成方案吗？
  • Does a solution exist in Apache Commons?Apache Commons 里有现成方案吗？
  • Are there any other libraries in the project already that solve this problem?项目里已经引入的其他库能解决吗？
  • Are there any open source libraries that solve this problem?有没有开源库已经解决了这个问题？
原书第 62 页

If you answered no to all the questions, you’re in the clear to write the code, making sure to use tests as you go along! If you answered yes to any of the questions, congratulations, you just saved yourself a lot of time; leverage what’s available!

如果所有问题你都答“没有”，那你就可以放心写代码了——记得边写边写测试！如果任何一个问题你答“有”，恭喜你，你刚给自己省了大量时间；直接用现成的吧！

That said, yesterday’s best practices are often tomorrow’s anti-patterns, and just because something was the right thing to do five or ten years ago doesn’t mean it is still the right thing to do today. Never be afraid to ask why, to challenge the status quo. You may find yourself mindlessly copying patterns or approaches you find or becoming complacent with code generated from AI without fully understanding why. Software moves pretty fast; if you don’t stop and look around once in a while and deliberately adopt an open perspective, you could miss some really important things (see “The Value of a Fresh Set of Eyes” on page 7). Languages, frameworks, technologies, and techniques are constantly evolving; keeping up is par for the course as a software engineer. Ask probing questions and keep a weather eye on the horizon.

话虽如此，昨天的最佳实践往往就是明天的反模式；某件事五到十年前是对的，不代表今天仍然对。永远别怕问为什么、别怕挑战现状。你可能会发现自己在盲目复制看到的模式或做法，或者对 AI 生成的代码心安理得、却没完全搞懂为什么。软件变得很快；如果你不停下来偶尔环顾四周、刻意保持开放的视角，可能会错过一些真正重要的东西（见第 7 页“一双新鲜眼睛的价值”）。语言、框架、技术和手法都在不断演进；作为软件工程师，跟上去是本分。多问探询性的问题，眼观六路耳听八方。

What Is Good Code?

All that aside, there won’t always be a library or language feature to solve your problem. You will, of course, write code! And you may ask yourself, well, what is good code? To paraphrase Potter Stewart, good code can be hard to define, but you know it when you see it. Admittedly, good versus bad code can be a very subjective concept. After a while, you start to develop a sense for it, and you may even say code has a smell to it. For example, overly long methods are generally a bad thing, but you still need to examine the code; there may not be a simpler approach. Few developers will ever admit to writing bad code, but anyone who’s ever opened an editor is guilty of some less-than-stellar software.

撇开这些不谈，不会总有库或语言特性来解决你的问题。你当然还是要写代码！于是你可能会问：到底什么是好代码？套用 Potter Stewart 的话：好代码很难定义，但你看到它就知道。诚然，好代码与坏代码可以是个非常主观的概念。过一段时间，你会开始培养出一种直觉，甚至会说代码有“味道”。例如，过长的方法通常不是好事，但你仍需具体看代码——也许并没有更简单的写法。很少有开发者会承认自己写过糟糕的代码，但每个打开过编辑器的人，都写过一些不那么光鲜的软件。

Metrics can provide insight into your codebase. For example, cyclomatic complexity can tell you the number of paths within your source code, with more paths indicating more complex code that would likely benefit from refactoring. Many languages have source code analyzers like PMD, SonarQube, and JSHint, which can help prevent certain types of bugs and bad coding practices from infesting the source code. Tools like SonarQube and CodeScene can provide invaluable insight into your codebase. Odds are your organization has something. If you’re not sure, ask around. If it doesn’t, why not spearhead the effort to bring one into your project?

指标能给你的代码库提供洞见。例如，圈复杂度能告诉你源码里有多少条路径，路径越多说明代码越复杂，往往值得重构。许多语言都有 PMD、SonarQube、JSHint 之类的源码分析器，能帮你防止某些类型的 bug 和坏味道在源码里滋生。SonarQube、CodeScene 这类工具能给你的代码库提供无比宝贵的洞见。你的公司多半已经有某种工具。不确定就问问；如果没有，为什么不由你牵头给项目引入一个呢？

Adding Metrics to Existing Projects
给既有项目加指标

In a perfect world, your project would leverage analysis tools like those mentioned from the very start of your project. Doing so allows your code to “start clean, stay clean” (assuming your colleagues fix the detected problems). However, you won’t always have that luxury, and you’ll have to add a linter or a source code analyzer to a project that has been in development for months or years.
在理想世界里，你的项目会从一开始就用上前面提到的那些分析工具。这样能让代码“从干净开始，保持干净”（前提是同事们把发现的问题修掉）。然而你不会总有这种奢侈；你往往要给一个已经开发了几个月甚至几年的项目临时加上 linter 或源码分析器。
It is tempting to add a tool like PMD and turn on all the rules! Do not do that. First of all, some of the rules contradict themselves; if one passes, another will fail. Second, turning on too many rules will typically result in an unmanageable number of warnings, which is counterproductive. It can demoralize a team. With hundreds or thousands of warnings, it is hard to notice when someone checks in code that adds a few more, and spending a few hours of effort to fix a couple of dozen warnings moves the graph an imperceptible couple of pixels.
装上 PMD 之类的工具就把所有规则全开？千万别。首先，有些规则自相矛盾；这条过了那条就得挂。其次，开太多规则通常会导致警告多到无法收拾，适得其反，还会打击团队士气。成百上千条警告摆在那儿，谁又多提交了几条根本注意不到；花几小时修掉几十条警告，图上也就挪动不起眼的几个像素。
Instead, have a discussion with your team and pick a few rules that you can all agree on. Finding that subset may prove challenging! Turn those rules on. That should result in a manageable number of warnings. As a team, work to fix them. Once you have done so, turn on a couple of more rules. Rinse and repeat. After a few months, you’ll have a rich set of rules running against your project as well as cleaner code.
相反，和团队讨论一下，挑出几条大家都认同的规则。找出这个子集可能就不容易！把这几条打开，警告数量应该可控。团队一起把它们修掉。修完再开几条规则，如此循环。几个月后，你就有了一整套规则在跑，代码也更干净了。

Metrics should never be mindlessly followed; some complexity just can’t be avoided! You must apply common sense to any rule of thumb because, in some instances, applying the common rule may actually make things worse. However, you can take advantage of the Hawthorne effect, which says people modify their behavior when they’re observed.2 You can absolutely use that to your advantage on a project! For example, if you want more of the code to be covered by tests, prominently display the code coverage stats.

指标绝不能盲从；有些复杂性就是不可避免的！对任何经验法则都要运用常识，因为在某些情况下，套用常识反而会把事情搞糟。不过，你可以利用霍桑效应——它说的是，当人们被观察时会改变自己的行为。2你完全可以在项目里利用这一点！例如，如果你希望更多代码被测试覆盖，就把代码覆盖率统计醒目地展示出来。

2 Like on the freeway when people notice the state trooper in the median and everyone slows down.
就像在高速公路上，人们注意到中间隔离带里有州警，于是所有人都慢了下来。

Increasing Code Coverage Through Metrics
用指标提升测试覆盖率

Nate here again. Many years ago, I joined a project that had been churning out code for a few months. I was pleasantly surprised there were, in fact, tests, but I was disappointed that all but a small handful were skipped by the build because they “kept failing.” Not to be deterred, I ran a code coverage report showing how many lines of code were executed after running all of the tests. Unsurprisingly, it was a single-digit number. But I posted it, and I talked about it. A lot. During most standups and retrospectives. Whenever the number ticked up, I heaped praise on my awesome teammates.
又是我 Nate。多年前，我加入了一个已经写了几个月代码的项目。让我惊喜的是，项目里居然有测试；但让我失望的是，除了寥寥几个，其他全被构建跳过了，因为它们“老是挂”。我没有气馁，跑了一份代码覆盖率报告，显示跑完所有测试后执行了多少行代码。毫不意外，是个位数。但我把它贴了出来，而且常拿出来说——大多数站会和回顾会上都讲。每当数字涨一点，我就把赞美的话毫不吝啬地送给我那些超棒的队友。
When someone added tests to a particularly tricky part of the code, I had them discuss how they did it. Slowly but surely, our code coverage number went up, and the code became less brittle. It took several months, but by the time I moved on to the next project, the code was closing in on 70% coverage. By no means were we satisfied, but we were in a far better place. And it all started by running—and then promoting—a simple code coverage report.
当有人给一段特别棘手的代码补上测试时，我会让他分享是怎么做的。慢慢地、稳稳地，我们的代码覆盖率数字上去了，代码也没那么脆弱了。这花了几个月时间，但等我离开那个项目时，覆盖率已逼近 70%。我们当然不满足，但处境已大为改观。而这一切，都始于跑一份简单的代码覆盖率报告——然后把它宣传出去。
原书第 64 页

Metrics can be abused or misused (see “Metrics Can Mislead” on page 19). For example, many organizations have tried to evaluate technical staff by lines of code written or deleted or modified. Use these metrics wisely. Consider external coupling or how many classes are dependent on a given class as another example. In general, if you see a high degree of coupling, you would consider that an opportunity for refactoring. What if that class is actually a facade that is essentially hiding a set of classes? You must contextualize any metric.

指标可以被滥用或误用（见第 19 页“指标会误导人”）。例如，许多公司曾试图用写了、删了、改了多少行代码来考核技术人员。请明智地使用这些指标。再举个例子：外部耦合，即有多少类依赖某个类。一般来说，如果你看到高度耦合，会把它当作重构的机会。但万一那个类其实是个门面（facade），本质上隐藏了一组类呢？你必须把任何指标放回具体情境里看。

Just because you can measure something doesn’t mean it will provide meaningful insights. Try to link metrics to project goals and focus on the direction your metrics trend. Are you getting better or worse over time? Favor short time horizons and be ready and willing to adjust and adapt.

能测量某样东西，不代表它就能提供有意义的洞见。尽量把指标和项目目标挂钩，关注指标的变化趋势。你是在变好还是变坏？倾向于看较短的时间窗，并随时准备调整适应。

Adding new tools to your pipeline isn’t your only choice. Many IDEs will provide code-quality metrics, and there are any number of plug-ins you could add to your personal toolchain that will help you write better code. To shorten the feedback loop, many of the code analysis tools can be wired into your editor, notifying you of violations as you type instead of waiting for a build break. Your team may have a preferred configuration. Ask a colleague if you aren’t sure.

往流水线里加新工具不是你唯一的选择。许多 IDE 会提供代码质量指标，你的个人工具链也可以加各种插件帮你写更好的代码。为了缩短反馈回路，许多代码分析工具可以接进编辑器，让你边敲边提示违规，而不用等构建挂掉。你的团队可能有偏好的配置。不确定就问同事。

Less Is More

The goal of software design is to create chunks or slices that fit into a human mind. The software keeps growing, but the human mind maxes out, so we have to keep chunking and slicing differently if we want to keep making changes.
——Kent Beck

软件设计的目标，是切分出能放进人脑的块或片。软件在不断长大，而人脑有极限，所以如果我们还想继续改，就得不断换方式切块分片。
——Kent Beck

With the size of some codebases, you might think developers are paid by the character. While some problems genuinely require millions of lines to solve, in most cases you should favor smaller codebases. The less code, the less there is to load into people’s brains. Many projects reach the size where it is no longer possible for one developer to understand all of the code, which is one of the forces that has given rise to microservices and functions as a service.

看着某些代码库的规模，你会以为开发者是按字符数领工资的。虽然有些问题确实需要上百万行才能解决，但在大多数情况下，你应该偏好更小的代码库。代码越少，要装进人脑的东西就越少。许多项目大到一个开发者已无法理解全部代码，这正是催生微服务和函数即服务的动力之一。

原书第 65 页

The typical big balls of mud often have dictionary-sized Getting Started guides and build processes that are measured by weeks and revolutions of the moon. It can take developers new to the project weeks or months to get productive within the code. The smaller the codebase, the less time it takes for a new developer to get their head wrapped around the code and the faster they can start contributing; see Chapter 6 for more details. The following are things to consider when trying to get your code length under control.

典型的“大泥球”项目，往往配有字典那么厚的入门指南，构建流程要按星期甚至按月来算。新加入项目的开发者可能要花几周甚至几个月才能在代码里产出价值。代码库越小，新人搞懂代码的时间越短，能开始做贡献就越快；详见第 6 章。以下是控制代码长度时要考虑的事情。

The Zeroth Law of Computer Science

Many of the practices software engineers espouse in an effort to tame code boil down to the zeroth law of computer science: high cohesion, low coupling. Cohesion is a measure of how things relate to one another. High cohesion means essentially that like things are together. The notification function that also contains print logic would be an example of low cohesion. Coupling refers to the amount of interdependence between modules or routines. Code with tight coupling can be difficult to modify as changes to one part of the code unexpectedly affect other, seemingly unrelated parts of the system. Changing the notification service shouldn’t break the print module. High cohesion and low coupling tend to result in code that is more readable and simpler to maintain and evolve. Many patterns are ways of achieving high cohesion and low coupling, often at different levels of abstraction. At their best, arguably, microservices are high cohesion, low coupling applied to services.

软件工程师为驯服代码而推崇的许多实践，归根结底都可以归结为计算机科学第零定律：高内聚、低耦合。内聚衡量的是一个事物内部各元素之间的关联程度。高内聚，本质上就是把相关的东西放在一起。一个通知函数里还塞着打印逻辑，就是低内聚的例子。耦合指的是模块或例程之间相互依赖的程度。紧耦合的代码难以修改，因为对某一部分的改动会出乎意料地影响系统中其他看似不相干的部分。改通知服务不应该把打印模块搞挂。高内聚低耦合的代码往往更可读、更易维护和演进。许多设计模式都是在不同抽象层次上实现高内聚低耦合的手段。可以说，微服务在最佳状态下，就是把高内聚低耦合应用到了服务层面。

Beware Boilerplate Code

Boilerplate code, even if it is generated by an editor or a framework, should be avoided. While you may not have to write it, you will still carry it around for the lifetime of the project. Classes should be short, a few pages or less.3 Programming languages will impact your definition of short, as some languages are more verbose than others. In general, if you have to scroll, your class might be too long.

样板代码，哪怕是编辑器或框架自动生成的，也应当避免。虽然你不用亲手写它，但它会跟着你一辈子——贯穿整个项目生命周期。类应当短小，几页以内。3不同语言对“短”的定义不同，因为有些语言比另一些更啰嗦。一般来说，如果你得滚动屏幕，这个类可能就太长了。

3 Though with modern monitor sizes, you may want to stick to a single page.
不过以现在显示器的尺寸，你也许该坚持控制在一屏以内。

Favor Composition over Inheritance

Many languages allow classes to inherit from other classes, and while this feature can be very powerful and there certainly is is-a relationships (a cat is a mammal) in software, it tends to be overused. Some developers use inheritance as a reuse mechanism. Reuse is a byproduct, not a rationale!

许多语言允许类继承其他类。虽然这个特性非常强大，软件里也确实存在“是一个”（is-a）关系（猫是哺乳动物），但它往往被过度使用。有些开发者把继承当作一种复用机制。复用是副产品，而不是理由！

原书第 66 页

Let’s look at a concrete example. Say your domain involves cars and trucks. You might create a vehicle superclass that cars and trucks both descend from that includes a combustion engine—since all cars and trucks have a combustion engine, defining it on the superclass ensures that all cars and trucks also have a combustion engine. For example, see this Ruby pseudocode:

来看一个具体例子。假设你的领域涉及轿车和卡车。你可能会建一个 Vehicle 父类，让轿车和卡车都继承它，里面包含一个内燃机——既然所有轿车和卡车都有内燃机，把它定义在父类上就保证了它们都有。例如下面这段 Ruby 伪代码：

class Vehicle {
    Engine engine
    Integer num_wheels
    Integer num_doors
    Function brake {}
    Function accelerate {}
}

class Truck < Vehicle {
    Number tow_capacity
}

class ElectricVehicle < Vehicle {
    Number range
    # wait… EVs don’t have engines…
}

But along come electric vehicles with nary a combustion engine to be found. An EV is-a vehicle, but not like those other vehicles. Composition is more flexible and should be favored over inheritance. That isn’t to say you should never use inheritance, just that you should prefer composition.

可电动车型来了，身上连个内燃机的影子都找不到。电动车确实“是一种”车，但又和别的车不一样。组合更灵活，应当优先于继承。这不是说你永远不该用继承，而是说你应当偏好组合。

Favor Short Methods

Write short methods, as in single-digit lines of code. Like a Linux or Unix command-line tool, methods should do one thing and only one thing, and they should do it well, working in concert to accomplish larger goals. Any method name that includes conjunctions (and, or, but) is a sign the method is doing too much. Method names should be clear and concise and avoid being clever. If you are having a hard time naming a method, it might be doing too much. Try breaking it apart and see what happens. Be descriptive. Remove logic duplication, even in small amounts. Simplify, then simplify some more.

写短方法，短到个位数行。像 Linux/Unix 命令行工具一样，方法应该做一件事、只做一件事，而且把它做好，再协同起来完成更大的目标。方法名里只要出现了连词（and、or、but），就说明这个方法做的事太多了。方法名应当清晰简洁，别耍聪明。如果你苦苦想不出方法名，它可能就是做太多了。试着拆开看看会怎样。要 descriptive。消除逻辑重复，哪怕量很小。简化，再简化。

Overall, aim for smaller, more manageable codebases to improve developer understanding and productivity.

总的来说，以更小、更易管理的代码库为目标，提升开发者的理解度和生产力。

Write Code to Be Read

Think about the developer who will follow in your footsteps, the one who will need to read and maintain your code. Remember to apply the Golden Rule to your code (see “Apply the Golden Rule to Software” on page 11). How could you write the code so that you make life better for the next developer? What do you need to communicate to the next person?

想一想那个将循着你足迹而来、需要阅读和维护你代码的开发者。记得把金科玉律用到代码上（见第 11 页“把金科玉律用到软件上”）。你该怎样写代码，才能让下一个开发者的日子更好过？你需要向下一个人传达什么？

原书第 67 页

There are any number of guidelines you can apply when it comes to the “correct” length of a function, from reuse to picking an often arbitrary number of lines. Martin Fowler offers sage advice: mind the separation between intent and implementation. In other words, how long does it take for you to understand what a function is doing? You should be able to read the name and understand immediately what the code does without investigating the method body itself. This principle will often lead to functions with only a few or even just a single line of code; make the intention clear. The class name should give you context, and the method names help you understand what the class does.

关于函数的“正确”长度，你可以套用无数条准则，从“复用”到拍脑袋定一个行数。Martin Fowler 给过一个睿智的建议：留意意图与实现的分离。换句话说，你要花多久才能看懂一个函数在做什么？你应该能只读函数名就立刻明白代码在做什么，而不必去翻方法体本身。这条原则往往会导向只有几行、甚至只有一行代码的函数——把意图表达清楚。类名应当给你上下文，方法名帮你理解这个类是做什么的。

Code can be written like a newspaper article with an “inverted pyramid.” Articles start with the lede then move to key facts and then on to deeper background. You, as the reader, can stop at whatever level of detail you wish—maybe just the first couple of paragraphs, maybe all the way to the end. As they say in publishing, don’t bury the lede.

代码可以像报纸文章那样用“倒金字塔”来写。文章先放导语，再给关键事实，最后是更深的背景。作为读者，你想停在哪个细节层级都可以——也许只读头两段，也许一路读到尾。正如出版界常说的：别把导语埋了。

Code should follow the same model. The class name is almost like the headline of an article. From there you should be able to skim the method signatures to get a general understanding. If you want to explore a function or a call to another class, you are free to do so, but you should still understand the gist of the code.

代码也应遵循同样的模式。类名几乎就像文章的标题。从那里你应当能浏览方法签名获得大致理解。如果你想深入某个函数或对另一个类的调用，尽可以去看，但你仍应能抓住代码的主旨。

Naming Things Is Hard
起名是难事

Every developer has stared at their editor struggling to name a variable, method, or class. And while this struggle can indicate an insufficient understanding of the problem or some overly complex code, there is a reason foo, bar, and foobar are such common occurrences. Coming up with meaningful names can be time-consuming. Don’t rush! Again, take the time it takes so it takes less time. It is worth the effort to come up with good names. Don’t be afraid to reach out to a teammate for their input. Sometimes just explaining what you’re working on will be enough to inspire the perfect moniker.
每个开发者都曾盯着编辑器，苦苦想给一个变量、方法或类起名字。这种挣扎既可能说明你对问题理解不足，也可能说明代码过于复杂——而 foo、bar、foobar 之所以如此常见，也是有原因的。起一个有意义的名字很耗时。别急！再说一遍，该花的时间花到位，往后才更省时间。花力气起个好名字是值得的。别害怕找队友征求意见。有时仅仅是把你在做的事讲一遍，就足以激发那个完美的名字。
Your IDE can help! Many developers work backward from the declaration, allowing the editor to make suggestions. In other words, start with new Arrays.asList({"Red", "Green", "Blue"});. Your IDE can use a postfix completion to suggest a variable name. Agentic coding tools can also provide some inspiration. Don’t hesitate to refactor poorly named code. Modern editors have powerful tools that make renaming a straightforward endeavor. Just make sure you aren’t constantly renaming core domain concepts, because that usually indicates a problem of misconception.
你的 IDE 能帮忙！许多开发者从声明往回写，让编辑器给建议。换句话说，先写 new Arrays.asList({"Red","Green","Blue"});，IDE 可以用后缀补全来建议变量名。智能体编码工具也能提供一些灵感。别犹豫，去重构命名糟糕的代码。现代编辑器有强大的工具，重命名是一件直截了当的事。只是要确保你不是在反复重命名核心领域概念——因为那通常意味着认知上出了问题。
It may also help to play the gibberish game. Often the first word you use to define a concept isn’t the best option, but it may shape your thinking about the problem domain. When you are first working through the domain, make up a word! After you’ve done some additional analysis, go ahead and replace the gibberish with real words. You’ll likely have come up with something that’s very different, and clearer, than your first reaction. The next time you’re really stuck on what to call something, throw in some nonsense words and circle back.
玩“胡话游戏”也可能有帮助。你用来定义一个概念的第一个词，往往不是最佳选择，但它会塑造你对问题域的思考。刚琢磨领域时，先编一个词！等做了更多分析，再把胡话换成真正的词。你很可能会得到一个和第一反应截然不同、却更清晰的结果。下次你实在想不出该叫什么时，先塞几个无意义的词进去，过一会儿再回来。

The Problem with Code Comments

Every programming language has some facility for a developer to speak, not to the compiler or runtime, but to their fellow developers via a code comment. And while it may seem like one should liberally comment their code, arguably doing so is a code smell.4 Code comments violate the DRY principle, aka Don’t Repeat Yourself. While you will most often see DRY violated with code that is copied and pasted or littered with logic duplication, comments can also be problematic. In most cases, you wrote the code and then you turned around and wrote about the code.

每门编程语言都提供了一种机制，让开发者不是对编译器或运行时说话，而是通过代码注释对 fellow 开发者说话。虽然看起来应该多写注释，但可以说，这么做本身就是一种代码坏味道。4代码注释违反了 DRY 原则——即“不要重复自己”。虽然 DRY 最常被复制粘贴的代码或重复逻辑破坏，但注释也可能成问题。大多数情况下，你写了代码，然后又转过身来写关于代码的描述。

4 You can often tell the experience level of a developer by their use (or avoidance) of code comments.
往往通过一个开发者用（或不用）代码注释的方式，就能判断他的经验水平。

Code comments can be a maintenance headache as well. You modify the code, but will you take the time to update the comments too? Often the comments begin diverging from the code, adding another layer of sediment to the developers who encounter the code months or years later. Code should be written to be readable. Your time is better spent making the code simpler to read than in documenting what you did. Expressive languages definitely aid in achieving readable code, and you may want to avoid the more nuanced “magic” features of your language of choice. Good method and variable names are better than comments; if you think you need to write a comment, try renaming the method or variable. Doing so will nearly always obviate the need for a comment.

代码注释也是维护上的头疼事。你改了代码，会花时间同步改注释吗？注释往往开始与代码脱节，给几个月或几年后碰到这段代码的开发者又添了一层沉积。代码应当写得可读。把时间花在让代码更易读上，比记录你做了什么更值。表达力强的语言无疑有助于写出可读代码，你也许还该避开所用语言中那些比较晦涩的“魔法”特性。好的方法名和变量名胜过注释；如果你觉得需要写注释，试试重命名方法或变量。这样做几乎总能让注释变得多余。

Arguably, the least useful code comment is the code change blocks that are often the first few hundred (or thousand) lines in a file. And while it can be an interesting waypoint along your archeological journey, the repetition of tracking numbers, dates, names, and paragraphs about the change adds noise to the process. Let your source code management tool do its job.

可以说，最没用的代码注释就是那种改动记录块——它们常常占据一个文件开头几百（甚至几千）行。虽然这在你的考古之旅中可以是个有趣的路标，但那一堆重复的单号、日期、人名和改动说明段落，只会给过程增加噪音。让你的源代码管理工具干它该干的事吧。

That isn’t to say code should never have comments.5 If you are doing something that isn’t obvious, and you couldn’t find a way to simplify the code, comments explaining the situation can be helpful. These comments should focus on why you did something instead of what you did. Providing context around a choice of one algorithm over another or explaining a particularly complex bit of logic can be helpful as well. That said, if code needs to be explained, rewrite it.

这倒不是说代码永远不该有注释。5如果你在做一件不那么显而易见的事，又找不到简化代码的办法，解释情况的注释会有帮助。这类注释应当聚焦于你为什么这么做，而不是你做了什么。在选择某一种算法而非另一种时给出上下文、或解释一段特别复杂的逻辑，也会有帮助。话虽如此，如果一段代码需要解释，那就重写它。

5 Dogmatism, whether in software or life, is rarely the right path. Favor pragmatism.
无论在软件还是生活中，教条主义都很少是正确道路。请务实。
原书第 69 页

Comments can serve as reminders to our future selves, or as a warning that a hack works but you don’t (yet) understand why it does. Some developers leave comments as warnings to future developers, as in the following example:

注释可以充当给未来自己的提示，或者警告：某个 hack 能跑，但你（还）不知道它为什么能跑。有些开发者会留下注释警告后来者，如下面这个例子：

// Dear maintainer:
//
// Once you are done trying to
// “optimize” this routine,
// and have realized what a terrible
// mistake that was,
// please increment the following
// counter as a warning
// to the next person:
//
// total_hours_wasted_here = 42

Are these comments a good thing? It depends, and many of the examples you will hear of are likely apocryphal. That said, don’t shy away from leaving behind advice for future you.

这类注释是好事吗？看情况，而且你听到的很多例子多半是杜撰的。尽管如此，别不好意思给未来的自己留点忠告。

Tests as Documentation

If comments aren’t an appropriate way to document code, what should you do? Write tests. Tests, especially those written in more fluent styles, are executable specifications that evolve along with the production code.6 Documentation, whether code comments, READMEs, or specifications, tends to diverge from the code as soon as it’s written. Tests written while you write code allow you to refactor freely and increase your confidence in the quality of your application. They also act as signposts for the developers who follow you. Testing is explored in more depth in Chapter 5.

如果注释不是记录代码的恰当方式，那该怎么做？写测试。测试，尤其是用更流畅的风格写的测试，是随生产代码一同演进的可执行规格说明。6文档——无论是代码注释、README 还是规格说明——往往一写出来就开始和代码脱节。边写代码边写测试，能让你自由重构，并提升对应用质量的信心。它们也为后来的开发者充当路标。测试在第 5 章会深入探讨。

6 Libraries like Spring REST Docs can also help documentation stay in sync with the code.
Spring REST Docs 之类的库也能帮文档与代码保持同步。

Adding tests to existing code allows you to capture what you’re learning about how the code works and unlocks your knowledge such that other developers can benefit from your work. As you rename a method or variable and prune some dead code, you’re actively leaving the code better than you found it.

给既有代码补测试，能让你把“代码是怎么工作的”这份学习成果记录下来，并把你的知识释放出来，让其他开发者也能受益。当你重命名方法或变量、清理死代码时，你就是在主动把代码改得比你发现它时更好。

Some developers insist they need to write copious comments for those who consume their services. While these comments are less smelly than those mentioned earlier, they aren’t your only option. Again, tests make for a more resilient documentation mechanism. Utilizing consumer-driven contracts allows you to convey what your service does while also giving you the confidence to iterate as necessary. As long as you haven’t violated the contract, you can evolve your code freed from the worry that you might inadvertently break a downstream system. Consumers gain confidence in your services, as they have a set of tests they can execute that simulates the expected behavior of your code. They can modify their code without fear of introducing a new defect.

有些开发者坚持要为服务的调用方写大量注释。虽然这类注释比前面说的那些味道小些，但并不是你唯一的选择。再说一遍，测试是更有韧性的文档机制。利用消费者驱动契约，既能传达你的服务做什么，又能让你放心地按需迭代。只要不违反契约，你就可以演进代码，而不必担心不小心搞挂下游系统。调用方也会对你的服务更有信心，因为他们有一组可执行的测试来模拟你代码的预期行为。他们改自己的代码时也不必担心引入新缺陷。

Consumer-driven contracts are a vital part of reliable and resilient software. Many languages and frameworks have projects you can (and should!) leverage with your applications. From Spring Cloud Contract to Pact versions for nearly every platform, you have options.

消费者驱动契约是可靠、有韧性的软件的重要组成部分。许多语言和框架都有你可以（而且应该！）在应用中使用的项目。从 Spring Cloud Contract 到几乎各平台都有版本的 Pact，你有的选。

Avoid Clever Code

Software is hard, and the domains you work in are complex. But not all complexity is equal. In his widely cited No Silver Bullet essay, Fred Brooks makes the distinction between accidental and essential complexity. In short, essential complexity is inherent in software, from the nuance of the business rules, to communicating with your team, to the ever-changing nature of a codebase. There is nothing you can do to remove this complexity from software; it comes with the paycheck. On the other hand, accidental complexity are ways developers make things harder than they have to be, from noisy technology to heavyweight tooling. When in doubt, keep it simple.

软件很难，你所处的业务领域也很复杂。但并非所有复杂性都一样。在被广泛引用的《没有银弹》一文中，Fred Brooks 区分了偶发复杂性和本质复杂性。简而言之，本质复杂性是软件固有的——从业务规则的细微差别，到与团队沟通，再到代码库不断变化的本性。你无法把这种复杂性从软件中消除；薪水就是为它付的。而偶发复杂性，则是开发者把事情弄得比实际更难的那些方式，从花哨的技术到笨重的工具。拿不准时，保持简单。

Software is not immune from the proverbial snake oil. Many companies attempt to sell products or processes that will revolutionize software delivery. It pays to be skeptical. There are opportunities for improvement of course, but the scientific method reminds us that extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence. You should be vigilant about removing accidental complexity wherever possible. See Chapter 6 for a more detailed discussion.

软件行业也不能免俗地充斥着所谓的“蛇油”。许多公司试图兜售号称能彻底变革软件交付的产品或流程。保持怀疑是值得的。当然改进空间总是有的，但科学方法提醒我们：非同凡响的主张需要非同凡响的证据。你应当时刻警惕，尽可能消除偶发复杂性。更详细的讨论见第 6 章。

Languages and frameworks often have error-prone forms. For example, take a look at the following Java code. Can you spot the problem?7 In Java, brackets are technically optional on a single-statement if block. Now, some developers might argue in favor of omitting the brackets, as it is less verbose and the (essentially) empty lines are a waste of vertical space. But what happens when another developer adds a second statement? Will they remember to add the brackets, or will they be seduced by the code indent?

语言和框架常有易错的写法。例如，看下面这段 Java 代码。你能发现问题吗？7在 Java 里，单语句 if 块在语法上可以省略大括号。有些开发者可能会主张省略大括号，因为这样更简洁，而那几行（基本）空行浪费纵向空间。但当另一个开发者加了第二条语句时会发生什么？他会记得加大括号，还是会被代码缩进迷惑？

if (condition)
  doFoo();
  doBar();
7 One of your authors, who shall remain nameless in this instance, spent the better part of two weeks debugging that code block.
本书一位作者（此处隐去其名）曾花了大半个两周来调试那段代码。

Avoid error-prone forms in your toolchain of choice. Just because you clearly understand it does not guarantee that the information is widely distributed across your team. Don’t be afraid to update (or establish) coding standards to cover these cases. There are a number of static analysis tools you can add to your deployment pipeline to keep you and your team from inadvertently introducing these types of problems. Take advantage of them.

在你选择的工具链里避免易错写法。你自己看得懂，并不保证这个理解在团队里人人都有。别害怕更新（或制定）编码规范来覆盖这些情况。你还可以往部署流水线里加若干静态分析工具，防止你和团队无意中引入这类问题。利用好它们。

Code Reviews

Code reviews can vary from asking a colleague for feedback on a method all the way to hours-long walk-throughs with several developers. Regardless of the specific implementation details, code reviews are an excellent way to learn, share experience, and socialize knowledge. More eyes on code is a good thing and part of the reason some organizations use pair programming.

代码评审可以小到请一位同事对某个方法给点反馈，也可以大到和几位开发者一起进行长达数小时的走读。无论具体形式如何，代码评审都是学习、分享经验和传播知识的绝佳方式。更多双眼睛看代码是件好事，这也是有些组织采用结对编程的部分原因。

Whether formal or not, certain practices can improve your code review. First and foremost, don’t be snarky. Avoid sarcasm. Asking for feedback can be very stressful for people, and many people take criticism personally. How you share your comments is critical. Be empathetic to your teammate. While it may be tempting to use a code review as an opportunity to drop some esoteric bit of trivia on your team, the goal is to improve the code, not exhibit your technical expertise.

无论正式与否，有一些做法能改进你的代码评审。首要的是：别阴阳怪气。避免讽刺。请人给反馈对当事人来说压力很大，而很多人会把批评往心里去。你怎么表达意见至关重要。对队友要有同理心。虽然你可能很想借代码评审的机会在团队里秀一段冷僻知识，但目标是改进代码，不是展示你的技术造诣。

The only way to make something great is to recognize that it might not be great yet. Your goal is to find the best solution, not to measure your personal self-worth by it.
——Jonas Downey, software designer, developer, and writer

把一件事做到卓越的唯一途径，是承认它现在可能还不够卓越。你的目标是找到最好的方案，而不是用它来衡量自我价值。
——Jonas Downey，软件设计师、开发者、作家

Focus your attention on the most important things. While style points matter, your effort is better spent lower down on the Code Review Pyramid. You can (and should) automate formatting and style-related issues;8 let a computer handle those. Your time and effort should be spent on the things computers can’t detect for you. Are method and variable names clear and concise? Is the code readable? Is there duplication? Does the code have the proper logging, tracing, and metrics? Are interfaces consistent with the rest of the code? Did the developer use any error-prone forms? Is the model correct? Did they choose the wrong abstraction?

把注意力集中在最重要的事情上。风格问题固然重要，但你的精力更应该花在代码评审金字塔更靠下的部分。格式和风格类问题你可以（而且应该）自动化；8让计算机去处理。你的时间和精力应当花在计算机替你发现不了的事情上：方法名和变量名清晰简洁吗？代码可读吗？有重复吗？代码有恰当的日志、链路追踪和指标吗？接口与代码其余部分一致吗？开发者有没有用易错写法？模型对吗？是不是选错了抽象？

8 Also known as “looks good to me” reviews, they aren’t a good use of a person’s time.
也叫“看起来不错就行”式评审，这是对人力的浪费。

Avoid the Checkbox Code Review

In some instances, code reviews are little more than a checkbox in the source code management system. Some organizations require all code to be reviewed before it is merged into the mainline. That goal may be admirable, but more often than not, it results in little more than one developer asking another to “review” the code, which usually means checking the box for their compatriot. Even though it comes from a good intention, such reviews defeat the purpose. Working in small batches makes reviews simpler and more effective.

在某些情况下，代码评审不过是源代码管理系统里的一个勾选框。有些组织要求所有代码合并到主干前必须经过评审。这个目标值得称赞，但结果往往不过是一个开发者请另一个开发者“评审”一下代码——而后者通常就是给自己的同胞打个勾。尽管出于好意，这种评审却背离了初衷。小批量工作能让评审更简单、更有效。

原书第 72 页

Some organizations use pull requests (PRs) as a way of ensuring code quality. While they can be more comfortable than spending the afternoon on a video call arguing over code, PRs aren’t always conducive to building team cohesion and trust. Some developers use PRs as an opportunity to nitpick, start a turf battle, or reignite a previously closed issue. PRs are also vulnerable to the LFTM (looks fine to me) response, which may be acceptable in some cases but falls victim to the previously mentioned checkbox review.

有些组织用拉取请求（PR）来保证代码质量。虽然 PR 比花一下午在视频会上争代码舒服些，但它并不总是有助于建立团队凝聚力和信任。有些开发者把 PR 当成吹毛求疵、挑起地盘之争、或重提已关闭议题的机会。PR 还容易沦为 LFTM（“看起来还行”）式回复——某些情况下可以接受，但终究是前面说的那种勾选式评审。

Text-based comments also lack the tone and body language of face-to-face conversations. You may not intend a comment to come across in an acidic or biting way, but it may be taken as such by the person on the other end of the request. Don’t be surprised if some of your teammates, especially those with less experience, dread a PR. Once again, practice empathy. Ask yourself how you’d like to be treated and act accordingly. Senior staff should lead by example.

基于文字的评论也缺少面对面交流中的语气和肢体语言。你可能并不想让评论显得尖酸刻薄，但请求另一端的人可能就这么解读了。如果你的一些队友（尤其是经验较少的）害怕 PR，别惊讶。再说一遍，要有同理心。问问自己希望被怎样对待，然后照做。资深员工应以身作则。

It Is Hard to Be Criticized

Developers often invest a lot of themselves into their work, so sometimes it is hard not to take feedback personally. Code reviews are not an opportunity to embarrass someone because they didn’t know about some new language feature or didn’t immediately see a simpler way to solve a problem. No one is perfect; everyone makes mistakes. Code reviews are about building better applications and are about the code, not the coder. Don’t get personal in a code review. Be humble and ask helpful questions. Critiques are more digestible when they are sandwiched by compliments, so be sure to point out the good things too.

开发者往往把大量自我投入到工作中，所以有时很难不把反馈往心里去。代码评审不是让谁难堪的场合——不要因为某人不知道某个新语言特性、或没立刻想到更简单的解法就让人下不来台。没有人是完美的；人人都会犯错。代码评审是为了构建更好的应用，关注的是代码，不是写代码的人。评审时别人身攻击。保持谦逊，问有帮助的问题。批评夹在表扬中间更容易下咽，所以也一定要指出做得好的地方。

Share your experiences. Personal stories carry immense weight and diffuse people’s natural resistance to change. Offer assistance with things you’ve encountered on previous projects. Be careful with blanket proclamations. Make sure you have all the details before you pronounce something won’t work, as you may be missing a key bit of context. Is there some background you don’t have? Perhaps there are constraints you aren’t aware of. Stick to the code.

分享你的经历。个人故事有巨大分量，能化解人们对改变的本能抵触。在你以前项目里遇到过的事情上提供帮助。别轻易下一概而论的断言。在你断言某件事行不通之前，先确认自己掌握了全部细节——因为你可能缺了关键的上下文。是不是有你不了解的背景？也许有你不知道的约束。紧扣代码本身。

Every single one of us is doing the absolute best we can given our state of consciousness.
——Deepak Chopra, Indian-American author and alternative medicine advocate

在我们各自的意识状态下，每一个人都已经在尽自己最大的努力。
——Deepak Chopra，印度裔美国作家、替代医学倡导者

If something in someone’s code concerns you, don’t be afraid to talk to the developer directly. People can be very defensive, especially in group situations. A quick one-on-one discussion could be the answer. Don’t ambush a teammate; no one wins in those interactions. Remember, reviews are a chance to learn, an opportunity to teach.

如果别人代码里有什么让你担心的地方，别害怕直接找那位开发者谈。人可能会非常防备，尤其是在群体场合。一次快速的一对一讨论可能就是答案。别伏击队友；那种互动里没有赢家。记住，评审是学习的机会，也是教人的机会。

原书第 73 页

Fostering Trust

If you shouldn’t do checkboxes or LFTM reviews, what should you do? Regardless of your code review process, don’t lose sight of its purpose. You should be sharing experiences, learning, and growing as a team while avoiding problematic practices like confusing idioms or deprecated approaches. Encourage your teammates to ask questions and provide constructive feedback. Code reviews should foster collective code ownership and foster trust among the team. Promoting a bug of the week or taking the time to share something you ran into can be incredibly powerful.

既然不该做勾选式或 LFTM 式评审，那该做什么？无论你的评审流程如何，都别忘记它的目的。你们应当作为一个团队分享经验、学习和成长，同时避开令人困惑的惯用法或已废弃的做法这类有问题的实践。鼓励队友提问、给出建设性反馈。代码评审应当培育集体代码所有权，增进团队间的信任。每周推一个“本周 bug”，或花点时间分享你踩过的坑，会非常有力量。

A regular meeting where people are encouraged to talk about an interesting defect they solved is an invaluable learning technique. You might assume everyone knows what to do when they encounter a particular issue, but discussing those situations with your teammates spreads knowledge. The simple act of taking time during Friday’s standup to discuss something interesting people experienced during the week can pay dividends.

定期开一个会，鼓励大家聊聊自己解决的某个有意思的缺陷，这是一种无价的学习手段。你可能以为每个人遇到某个特定问题时都知道怎么办，但和队友讨论这些情况能传播知识。就在周五站会上花点时间聊聊这周大家遇到的有趣事情，这个简单的举动就能带来丰厚回报。

It should go without saying, but treat your teammates with respect. Be kind, do what’s right, do what works. Don’t be afraid to take a moment to review your approach and ask if there might be a better way. Whether you’re following an Agile development methodology or not, you should adapt and adjust on a regular basis. If something isn’t working, change it!

不言而喻，请尊重你的队友。与人为善，做对的事，做有效的事。别害怕停下来审视自己的做法，问问是否有更好的方式。无论你是否遵循敏捷开发方法论，都应当定期调整适应。不管用，如果某件事不奏效，就改变它！

Learning New Languages

If you want to get better at writing code, you need to, well, write code. But you can accelerate those skills by learning new programming languages. Think about learning a foreign language. For months, even years, you will translate that language into your native tongue. Eventually, you will think, even dream, in your new language. But it takes time. Programming languages are no different. Well, they have very demanding grammar rules and far fewer keywords.

想提高写代码的能力，你就得——嗯——写代码。但你可以通过学习新的编程语言来加速这些技能。想想学一门外语：几个月甚至几年里，你都会把那门语言翻译成母语。最终，你会用新语言思考，甚至做梦。但这需要时间。编程语言也没什么不同。嗯，只不过它的语法规则更苛刻，关键字也少得多。

The key is immersion. If you really want to learn French, moving to Paris will accelerate your progress. Picking up a new programming language is much the same. Build an app in the new language that solves a problem that’s plagued you at work or at home. Follow the community on social media. Listen to the related podcasts or watch the videos from the latest conference focused on the language. Better yet, attend the local user group or go to the next event about the topic.

关键是沉浸。如果你真想学法语，搬到巴黎会加速你的进步。学一门新的编程语言也大同小异。用新语言写一个 app，解决一个在工作或家里困扰你的问题。在社交媒体上关注社区，听相关播客，看最新一届该语言大会的视频。更好的是，参加本地用户组，或去下一场相关活动。

Developers tend to get very attached to their first language. Be careful here. Programming languages are just tools. Just as a hammer is a better tool for pounding in a nail than a screwdriver, some languages are better fits for certain problems than others. For example, many embedded systems are written in C since it is highly portable and reliable and can be heavily optimized for specific platforms. Make it a habit to look at, explore, and learn other languages.

开发者往往会对自己的第一门语言产生很深的感情。在这点上要小心。编程语言只是工具。正如锤子比螺丝刀更适合钉钉子，某些语言比另一些更适合解决特定问题。例如，许多嵌入式系统用 C 编写，因为 C 高度可移植、可靠，还能针对特定平台重度优化。养成看一看、探索、学习其他语言的习惯。

原书第 74 页

Some influential people suggest learning a new language every year or two.

一些有影响力的人物建议每隔一两年就学一门新语言。

Programming Is Fundamentally About Communication
编程本质上是关于沟通的

Before computer science departments started springing up at universities around the world, programming often lived in the math department, and many assumed mathematical aptitude was a prerequisite for success in software. In some instances, universities still use math exams to recruit students! Despite this assumption, research shows that language aptitude is a far better predictor of how quickly someone picks up a new programming language than skill in mathematics. While certain domains may be very math heavy, the art of programming isn’t.
在世界各地大学开始纷纷设立计算机科学系之前，编程往往栖身于数学系，许多人以为数学天赋是在软件领域取得成功的先决条件。在某些地方，大学至今还在用数学考试招生！尽管有这样的假设，研究却表明：语言天赋比数学技能更能预测一个人掌握新编程语言的速度。虽然某些领域确实非常吃数学，但编程这门艺术并不吃。
Programming is first and foremost a communication activity—and not between the coder and the compiler. Don’t forget, the computer understands any code (at least if it’s syntactically correct), but that doesn’t mean a human will follow what you’re trying to accomplish. The best software engineers focus on the person reading the code. Good writers (of any kind) always keep the audience front of mind.
编程首先是一种沟通活动——而且不是编码者与编译器之间的沟通。别忘了，计算机能理解任何代码（至少在语法正确时），但这并不意味着人能跟上你想做的事。最优秀的软件工程师把注意力放在读代码的人身上。优秀的写作者（无论写什么）永远把读者放在心头。

Learning a new language takes time. How do you justify the investment it takes learning something you might not use daily at work? Learning a new language will change how you code even if you don’t get to use the new tool day in and day out. When you seek out a new language challenge, try to pick something that is different from what you use at work. If you’re an experienced Java developer, look beyond other C-like languages such as C# (not that there’s anything wrong with learning C#, mind you) toward different paradigms. Consider instead a dynamic language like Ruby or a functional language like Haskell. Trust us, even just a cursory examination of a language outside your normal neighborhood will fundamentally alter your approach to programming. You may come to appreciate your regular language more, or you may find yourself writing code in a different way. Take time to learn new things.

学一门新语言需要时间。你怎么为学习一样工作中可能并不每天用的东西找理由？哪怕你并不每天用这个新工具，学一门新语言也会改变你写代码的方式。当你想找一门新语言挑战时，尽量选和工作中用的不同的。如果你是经验丰富的 Java 开发者，别只盯着 C# 这类 C 系语言（注意，学 C# 没什么不好），而要看向不同的范式。不妨考虑 Ruby 这样的动态语言，或 Haskell 这样的函数式语言。相信我们，哪怕只是粗略浏览一下你熟悉圈子之外的语言，也会从根本上改变你的编程方式。你可能会更欣赏自己常用的语言，也可能会发现自己用不同的方式写代码。花时间学新东西。

Learning new languages gets easier over time. The more languages you know, the more you have to compare to. Think back to the first language you learned—you were starting at zero. By the third, fourth, fifth language, you start to see how one idiom is just like another one from Java, or how some structure was borrowed from Ruby.

学新语言会随时间变容易。你会的语言越多，可比较的对象就越多。回想你学的第一门语言——那是从零开始。到第三、第四、第五门时，你就会发现某个惯用法和 Java 里的一模一样，或某个结构是从 Ruby 借来的。

Early in your career, you should focus your attention on going as deep as you can on the languages and frameworks you use daily. However, don’t neglect exploring other options. Doing so will not only invigorate you but also make you a better developer.

职业生涯早期，你应把精力尽量深地投入到日常使用的语言和框架上。但也别忽略探索其他选择。这样做不仅能让你焕发活力，还会让你成为更好的开发者。

原书第 75 页

Wrapping Up

Developers write code; it is part and parcel of the job. Avoiding error-prone forms and overly clever code can be the difference between a codebase that’s a pleasure to work on and one that developers avoid like the plague. From code reviews to analysis tools, there are many ways to help you write better code. Favor writing tests over copious comments. When critiquing code, be empathetic. Never forget, code should be written to be read by humans; adhering to that principle goes a long way toward ensuring you write code others will stamp with the elusive “good” label!

开发者写代码；这是工作的应有之义。避开易错写法和过于聪明的代码，可能就是“一个让人乐于动手的代码库”与“开发者避之唯恐不及的代码库”之间的差别。从代码评审到分析工具，有很多方式帮你写出更好的代码。多写测试，少写注释。评审代码时要有同理心。永远别忘了：代码是写给人读的；坚守这条原则，你写的代码就很有希望被别人盖上那个 elusive 的“好”章！

Writing good code is an ongoing learning process. Be open to learning new skills and improving the ones you’ve already developed. Staying up-to-date on best practices in software engineering is a key to your long-term success in the field.

写好代码是一个持续的学习过程。保持开放，学习新技能、精进已有的技能。跟上软件工程最佳实践的最新进展，是你在这行长期成功的关键。

Putting It into Practice

There are no shortcuts; if you want to improve as a developer, you will need to write code! As the old joke goes: A pedestrian on 57th Street sees a musician getting out of a cab and asks, “How do you get to Carnegie Hall?” Without pause, the artist replies wearily, “Practice.” If you want to be a better developer, you need to practice.

没有捷径；想作为开发者进步，你就得写代码！就像那个老笑话：第五十七大街上，一个行人看到一位音乐家下出租车，问：“去卡内基音乐厅怎么走？”艺术家不假思索、疲惫地回答：“练习。”想成为更好的开发者，你就得练习。

Consider adding some effortful study to your routine. Periodically, say every other month or so, block out a couple of hours to tackle a code kata. In martial arts, katas are a series of blocks, kicks, and punches that students study and repeat countless times. Code katas bring this idea to software, providing simple problems that give you a chance to practice your craft and to work on things you may not encounter in your day-to-day coding life.

考虑在日常里加入一些刻意练习。每隔一段时间，比如大概每隔一个月，抽出两小时做一道 code kata（代码道场题）。在武术里，型（kata）是学生反复研习、演练无数次的一系列格挡、踢击和出拳。代码道场把这个理念带到软件领域，提供简单的题目，让你有机会磨练手艺，练习日常编码中可能遇不到的东西。

You can leverage code katas in any number of ways. You could pick one and solve it in two or three programming languages. You could pair with a friend or colleague to work through a kata. There are multiple ways to solve a given kata; challenge yourself to solve the same kata in two or three ways. Perform a code review on a kata you solved a few months (or years!) ago—what would you do differently today?

你可以用各种方式利用 code kata。挑一道，用两三种编程语言解出来。和朋友或同事结对一起做一道。一道 kata 有多种解法；挑战自己用两三种方式解同一道。对你几个月（甚至几年！）前做过的一道 kata 做一次代码评审——今天的你会怎么做 differently？

Once again, you can leverage the universe of open source software. Block out a couple of hours to contribute to an open source library you use (or want to use). If you’re not sure where to start, check out the trending repositories on GitHub. Contributing to open source is an excellent learning laboratory, and it isn’t nearly as hard to get started as you may think.9

再说一次，你可以利用整个开源宇宙。抽出两小时，给你用（或想用）的一个开源库做点贡献。不知道从哪开始？去看 GitHub 热门仓库。为开源做贡献是极好的学习实验室，而且入门远没有你想象的那么难。9

9 Many projects have lists of bugs marked as “for first-time contributors,” but don’t be afraid to reach out to the contributors; most will happily help you get up and running.
许多项目都有标记为“适合首次贡献者”的 bug 清单；也别害怕联系贡献者，大多数人会很乐意帮你跑起来。
原书第 76 页

You can still learn a tremendous amount about writing good code without contributing. Pick a project and spend a couple of hours reading through the code. What do you like? What don’t you like? What would you do differently? Run a source code analyzer against the code: what does that tell you about the project? If you see any glaring issues, don’t be afraid to raise them or contribute a PR!

即使不做贡献，你也能学到大量关于写好代码的东西。挑一个项目，花两小时通读代码。你喜欢什么？不喜欢什么？你会怎么做 differently？对代码跑一遍源码分析器：它告诉你关于项目的什么？如果发现什么扎眼的问题，别害怕提出来，或直接提个 PR！

Keeping up with change is a core component to a successful career in software; make it a habit to refresh your knowledge on your core languages and frameworks. You may not organically encounter new features in your daily work, so take a few hours once or twice a year to see what has been added to your toolkit. Most technologies have advocates or champions, so follow or subscribe to keep abreast of changes. Not every shiny new thing will work for your applications, at least today, but it is simpler to digest a small handful of updates periodically than to try to learn about dozens or hundreds of new things every few years.10

跟上变化是软件职业生涯成功的核心要素；养成定期刷新核心语言和框架知识的习惯。日常工作中你可能不会自然遇到新特性，所以每年抽一两次、每次几小时，看看你的工具箱里新增了什么。大多数技术都有布道者或代言人，关注或订阅他们以掌握动态。不是每个闪亮的新东西都适合你的应用（至少现在不适合），但定期消化一小撮更新，比每隔几年恶补几十上百个新东西要轻松。10

10 Something that also applies to upgrades to said technologies…
这句话同样适用于上述技术的升级……

Last but certainly not least, consider volunteering your coding talent to a local charity or nonprofit. Many deserving organizations are constantly looking for help from the technical community. Volunteering can give you a chance to practice your craft, maybe using a language or framework you’re trying to learn, while also helping a cause you care about.

最后但同样重要的是，考虑把你的编程才华志愿奉献给当地的慈善机构或非营利组织。许多值得帮助的组织一直在寻求技术社区的帮助。志愿活动能让你有机会磨练手艺——也许用上你正在学的语言或框架——同时帮助你在乎的事业。
